_doc: HARDCASTLE dating cabinet (#19, built 2026-07-18 — closes the Dunhill family cluster with parker.json). NO date codes, NO documented COM eras — Loring's verdict is encoded honestly: 'in the absence of sales receipts or other provenance, Hardcastles cannot be accurately dated'. What CAN be dated: the OWNERSHIP-ERA ladder (family -> Dunhill 49% 1936 -> Dunhill 100% 1946 -> Parker-Hardcastle 1967 with the Forest Road plant closed) + model-name era lists + the WWII horn-stem tell. SOURCE (local-first): staging/pipedia/Hardcastle.json (incl. Loring refs, Valitchka nomenclature photos, FinePipes 1944 6-day set). SOURCE-INTERNAL CONFLICT: intro says founded 1908, its own timeline says 1903 (Edmund Hardcastle) -> wide honest floor 1903, note kept. Never claim Dunhill production in a Hardcastle (Loring: indistinguishable, unlikely).

history_anchors._doc: 1903 (timeline) or 1908 (intro) — Edmund Hardcastle founds the brand; reputable British mid-grader. Forest Road, Walthamstow, London E17. 1935: Dunhill builds a factory NEXT DOOR. 1936: family sells 49% to Dunhill. 1946: Dunhill buys the rest (family still manages; Notting Hill Dunhill factory closes same year). 1967: merged with Parker -> PARKER-HARDCASTLE LIMITED (absorbs Masta Patent Pipe Co too); Forest Road plant given up, production moves to Parker's St Andrews Road factory; Edwin Hardcastle (last family executive) openly called the result 'an inferior Dunhill second'. Post-1967: speculated 'Parker seconds' brand; funneled-down bowls not fit for Dunhill/Parker stamps. 1982: Dunhill's OWN production moves into the Parker-Hardcastle Walthamstow factory (both firms listed at 32 St Andrews Rd E17). WWII: German vulcanite unavailable -> 1944 6-day set wears HORN stems, workmanship still first-rate.

brand_marks.physical: Family/Dunhill-era boxes and bags stamped Jack O'London (Forest Rd factory era sheets exist). WWII pipes may carry HORN stems (vulcanite shortage).

line_years._notes: FAMILY-PERIOD model list (pipedia) -> era 1903-1967 (ends at the Parker-Hardcastle merger; start = wide brand floor per the 1903/1908 conflict). DUNHILL-SECONDS model list (Start/Argyle/After Lunch/Crescent/Duke/Jockey Club/Scout) -> the Dunhill-ownership era; encoded 1946-1999 LOW-side-wide (list is undated; 1946 = 100% ownership; end approx). NOT encoded: start/crescent/duke (generic word collision), the table/dental/lightweight (generic), de luxe/straight grain (generic across brands). Loring rule: none of this is precise — provenance beats all.
